articles.title_orig: China Moves to Screen Patents Used in SRDI and “Little Giant” Enterprise Certification
articles.title_zh: China Moves to Screen Patents Used in SRDI and “Little Giant” Enterprise Certification
articles.content_orig:
On October 23, 2026, four Chinese government bodies – the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the State Taxation Administration , and the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) – jointly issued a notice titled “Notice on Further Preventing the Influence of Unscrupulous Intermediary Agencies on the Cultivation and Certification of High-Quality SMEs” ( 工信厅联企业〔2026〕40号 , dated October 13, 2026). The notice addresses the involvement of third-party intermediary agencies in assisting companies with preparation of application materials, including patent filings, for China’s Specialized, Refined, Distinctive, and Novel (SRDI, 专精特新) and “Little Giant” (小巨人) enterprise designations.
Patents are part of the evaluation criteria for both designations; the number of invention patents and PCT filings is incorporated into the SRDI development quality evaluation index. The notice states that this has contributed to cases in which patents are obtained or filed for the purpose of meeting numerical thresholds rather than for other purposes.
The notice directs provincial-level SME authorities to coordinate with intellectual property and taxation departments to strengthen verification of application data. It calls for the establishment of a “front-end patent screening mechanism” (专利前端排查机制), under which local intellectual property authorities will screen for abnormal patent situations during the SRDI SME and “Little Giant” certification process and evaluate patent quality as part of the review. The notice also directs authorities to explore use of artificial intelligence and big-data analysis tools to support reviewer work, and to maintain on-site verification procedures. Indicators identified for targeted review include anomalous metrics, inconsistent data, and sudden increases or decreases in reported figures, including patent counts.
The notice requires that certification review panels be assembled using a random selection process for both reviewers and task assignment, and bars intermediary agencies that provide application-preparation services from participating in review of the same applications. Companies found to have submitted falsified data or materials will have their designation revoked and will be barred from reapplying for three years. Intermediary agencies found to have engaged in conduct such as fabricating application materials, making false or misleading representations about certification outcomes, or using improper means to solicit clients are subject to joint enforcement by SME authorities, cyberspace regulators, and intellectual property authorities, with identified cases to be published on the national SME cultivation platform. MIIT stated it will continue to apply review measures through SME development quality evaluations, joint SME and high-and-new-technology enterprise (HNTE) inspections, and unannounced inspections of SRDI enterprises.
Companies designated as SRDI SMEs (专精特新中小企业) have been reported to gain eligibility for provincial and municipal subsidy programs, access to government procurement opportunities, preferential consideration for bank credit (including government-backed loan guarantee or interest-subsidy programs in some jurisdictions), inclusion in technology and standards pilot programs, and access to government-provided counseling and application support.
Companies designated as “Little Giant” enterprises (专精特新”小巨人”) have been reported to additionally receive one-time central government fiscal awards, with amounts subject to annual budget allocation, as well as local matching subsidies that in some jurisdictions have exceeded the central-level award. “Little Giant” status has also been cited by the Sci-Tech Innovation Board (科创板) and the Beijing Stock Exchange as a factor considered during listing review, and designated companies have been reported to gain access to specialized equity investment and development funds, including national-level SME development funds, as well as consideration for participation in national technology and industrial-chain project programs, including open-bidding R&D programs (“揭榜挂帅”).
The original text of the notice is available here (Chinese only).

articles.title_orig: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years
articles.title_zh: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years
articles.content_orig:
The Song dynasty sculptures were given to the National Gallery of Australia in the 1990s, a time when art theft was rife in China
Australia has returned two stone sculptures to China after more than 30 years abroad.
The statues, showing the heads of a military official and civil servant, had been given to the National Gallery of Australia in Canberra by a private collector and date back to the Northern Song dynasty (960–1127).
China’s National Cultural Heritage Administration received the heads on Wednesday, according to the state broadcaster CCTV.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft earnings live: Microsoft beats Q1 expectations on top and bottom line on AI growth
articles.title_zh: Microsoft earnings live: Microsoft beats Q1 expectations on top and bottom line on AI growth
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business.
Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business.
The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported  $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue.
For Azure, Hood said she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus.
"We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," the company's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts.
Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue.
Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues.
"In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said. The delays have to do with GPU-as-a-service providers, she said.
Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time.
Microsoft will continue to generate free cash flow through the 2027 fiscal year, but the company will access additional sources of funding when it's attractive to do so, Hood said.
"We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our rates ratings are, and sort of we haven't been able to — we haven't yet, I would say, tapped that," she said. "And then, of course, there's other options."
Microsoft's net income increased to $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million loss on its investment in OpenAI.
For the first time, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter, despite the delays from third-party providers.
Analysts polled by StreetAccount expected $32.32 billion. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
Microsoft reported results under two operating segments — Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.  For the past 11 years, the company had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
In Agents and Infra, revenue rose almost 25% to $76.8 billion, more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.
The number of people using the Microsoft 365 Copilot AI assistant is up 50% from last quarter, CEO Satya Nadella said on the call. The company did not disclose the number of paid seats. The recently announced high-end Microsoft 365 E7 productivity bundle now has millions of seats, Hood said.
Revenue in the Devices and Consumer business slipped 3% to $15.48 billion, beating the StreetAccount consensus of $15.05 billion. The unit includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers.
Sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%, as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. The company pointed to the end of support for Windows 10 last year and weak PC demand.
As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities.

articles.title_orig: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.title_zh: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.content_orig:
A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped in central Spain , derailing two cars and killing at least 68 people Wednesday morning, according to local authorities.
The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers continue searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies.
The crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, according to Spain's rail system operator ADIF. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.
Padilla told state broadcaster TVE the accident was between two high-speed trains heading in the same direction from Madrid to Seville and that one ran into the tail of the other while it was stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track.
The accident involved a train from Spain's state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO. Trains from those two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January. Padilla said 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers were in the IRYO train.
"Today all of Spain is grieving," Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning.
Sánchez called for increased safety measures to restore confidence in a high-speed rail system that was once a source of national pride.
"It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year," said Sánchez, who faces a national election on Nov. 29.
Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the crash was caused by what he called the "inexplicable" order from a central command center for Spain's trains after a security system had failed. He said the train engineers were not to blame.
Puente said that at 8:30 a.m. the security system on a stretch of 63 kilometers (39 miles) stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop. But the central command told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, and it ended up colliding with the stopped IRYO train at 8:53 a.m.
Puente said the train should never have been told to start moving again since there was still a "stop signal" active on that line. And if it had, at least it should have been told to go at reduced speed.
Authorities were still studying information to see how fast the train was going, but it could have been at 200 kph (124 mph) for that stretch of the track, Puente said.
"I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts," Puente said.
The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by olive fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left carriages shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said that emergency workers were focused on rescuing survivors and bodies from the most damaged train cars.
"It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," García said.
Passenger Ignacio Relaño was traveling on the RENFE train. He told state broadcaster TVE that the train had stopped momentarily on the line before it started again and then crashed into the IRYO.
"We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact," he said. "The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cell phones. Everything shook."
Another passenger recounted to Cadena Ser radio how she felt the train slam on the brakes and was thrown forward in her seat, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw body parts and trapped people covered in blood.
The mayor of the nearby town of Urda, Manuel Galán, told Spanish state broadcaster TVE that civil protection authorities had asked his town hall to prepare a sports pavilion to attend to passengers.
In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook the confidence the European country has in its extensive high-speed rail network.

articles.title_orig: King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
articles.title_zh: King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
articles.content_orig:
King addresses 'suffering and injustices' in Bahamas past
King Charles III has begun his tour of the Caribbean by acknowledging the "great suffering of the past" as he faced calls for slavery reparations.
Speaking an event in the Bahamas celebrating local youth, the King said the country's culture was "born out of darkness", and it was "only right" to acknowledge historic injustices.
His nine-day tour will culminate in the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), where the King has confirmed leaders will discuss the region's legacy of slavery.
The visit, his first as monarch, comes in the wake of renewed calls from Caribbean nations for Britain to apologise for its role in selling enslaved people for profit.
Prior to the trip, Buckingham Palace said the King would not shy away from "colonial legacy" and the impact of the slave trade during his visit but, in line with the UK government position, he will not apologise for Britain's role in the slave trade or offer reparations.
Upon his arrival on Tuesday, the King met Governor General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt and its Prime Minister Philip Edward Davis, before speaking with members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force as he inspected a guard of honour.
King Charles, wearing sunglasses and a grey suit, was then met with cheers as he arrived for his first engagement at a youth rally at Clifford Park - where he attended  independence celebrations for the Bahamas as Prince of Wales in 1973.
The young people in the crowd had been given time off school for the event. "It's my first time seeing him in person out of TikTok so he's out there, it's cool," one student told the BBC.
A small group of protesters gathered close to the rally shouting "pay us what you owe us" and "return artefacts you've stolen."
The group of around a dozen protesters was kept outside the main venue as they called on the King to help change the UK government's position on apologising and offering reparations.
"He's a man of influence. The Crown still has influence. And if they do not do it then we will become a republic and we will turn our backs on England if you do not show respect to the former colonies," said one protester, Sharon Purcer-Cooper.
The King spoke with young people as he attended his first engagement of the trip
The King spoke to these performers at a Nassau rally where the focus was on youth
The King spoke with Philip Edward Davis, Prime Minister of the Bahamas
During his speech in Nassau, the King acknowledged his 50-year-long commitment to fighting climate change and highlighted the challenges faced by low-lying Caribbean islands, saying that "our world cries out for healing".
He went on to call on young people at the rally to "take up the sacred task to play your part" as "in years to come, this will be surely be the measure of every person - how they answered the call to care for planet earth - the source of our life, our prosperity and our security".
The King resumes engagements in the Bahamas on Wednesday, where he will hear how vulnerable the low lying islands of the Caribbean are to climate change.
He will also learn more about the Bahamian tradition of Junkanoo - a cultural festival and street parade.
Buckingham Palace said opportunities for the King to reflect on the legacy of the slave trade will be built into the schedule of his nine-day tour of three Caribbean countries with visits planned to memorials and other places of reflection and remembrance.
A spokesperson for the palace told the BBC that the King's programme on the tour "will primarily focus on shining a light on the many modern partnerships and opportunities for the future", specifically those which are "having a transformative effect on the region".
For the King, the spokesperson added, the "tour is both a new journey but also the continuance of a lifelong one, in which he has sought to engage, understand and educate about the most shameful aspects of our past".
Those themes will be reflected by the King through the nine-day visit, the palace said.
The visit has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda with an emphasis on honouring the past but also looking forward to the ambition and possibility for future generations.
The King will move to Guyana later this week where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity.
He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where he will be joined by Queen Camilla, for the CHOGM and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth.
The biennial summit will bring together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.

articles.title_orig: Cruise line folds over fuel costs, booting passengers in Cambodia
articles.title_zh: Cruise line folds over fuel costs, booting passengers in Cambodia
articles.content_orig:
The Villa Vie Odyssey was more than 750 days into its voyage around the world when it came to a stop in Cambodia
A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia.
The US-based operator of the Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements".
It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world".
Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship's operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 (Â£6,000) from $1,800.
Villa Vie Residences said it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port". But those measures turned out to be insufficient to "offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs".
"Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," it said.
The company would spend the next 60 days on "restructuring and recapitalisation", though "no outcome is assured", it said.
There were reportedly around 200 passengers on board when they were ordered to disembark in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, a once sleepy beach town that has gained global notoriety in recent years as a hub for Chinese casinos and scam centres.
The Villa Vie Odyssey's voyage was expected to span 3.5 years and cover nearly 150 countries, according to its website.
Its departure had faced delays as the ship underwent repairs, leaving passengers stranded in Belfast for months and costing the company millions of pounds.
The ship was more than 750 days into its circumnavigation before announcing its suspension of its journey on Tuesday - which means its passengers would now be stranded in Cambodia.
Passengers Lanette Canen and Johan Bodin told the BBC they were informed by Villa Vie Residences' chief executive at 6am on Tuesday that they had to leave by 2pm on the same day.
The couple said passengers had known for some time about the company's financial difficulties. A potential investor had previously come onboard the ship to do due dilligence, but in the end it did not work out.
"Even then, we were still hoping a miracle investor would come through," they said. "Although there were signs that this would happen, we still felt disbelief when it became real. We were heartbroken. It felt like our dream had been crushed."
"There have been a lot of hugs and tears as residents support one another and process what has happened."
Another passenger Holly Hennessey said that the ship's passengers had earlier been asked to consider paying a fuel surcharge as global prices soared, and that their itinerary had been "severely curtailed".
Some people decided to disembark and travel on land, she said.
"It was not on my bingo card of places where I'd be spending a lot of time," Hennessey told the BBC from Cambodia.
"We're all in different hotels; there are a number of shipmates in the hotel that I'm in. We're just waiting."
Canen and Bodin said the location in Cambodia was "a difficult place to disembark" because of the distance to a major international airport.
Cruise passenger Holly Hennessey and her cat, Captain, have now found themselves in Cambodia
During their time onboard the Villa Vie Odyssey, passengers had access to several bars and restaurants, a pool deck and a pickleball court, according to its website.
Permanent residencies in its cabins ranged from $120,000 to $440,000. Those cabins were also available for rent from $3,500 a month.
Last year, the company launched a lifetime residence programme for people to spend their retirement years at sea.
In 2024, days after US President Donald Trump won his second term, Villa Vie Residences announced a four-year "Skip Forward" package.
Its CEO told Fox Business at the time that it was the "perfect product for those who said they'd leave the country if 'XYZ' wins the election".
For Canen and Bodin the experience was "worth it", despite the fact it was shorter than expected.
"We loved our two years on Odysseyâthe adventures, the places we visited and the friends we made along the way."
Many of the passengers have already made plans to "settle together off the ship, so those friendships and that sense of community are continuing on land", they said.
The couple plans to spend a few days in Sihanoukville, before travelling to different parts of South East Asia while they "figure out our next chapter".
But others, like Hennessey, have decided to stick around in Cambodia in the hopes that the Odyssey will set sail again soon.
"Until they say we are done - done done - I am not giving up. I could never duplicate this lifestyle. The idea of going home? It would be so trite," she said.
"Cambodia's not the worst place to hang out."

articles.title_orig: Fed leaves rates steady as governor Lisa Cook dissents
articles.title_zh: Fed leaves rates steady as governor Lisa Cook dissents
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after hiking borrowing costs in September to clamp down on inflation.
The central bank left the federal funds rate at a target range of 3.75% to 4%, keeping it unchanged after raising rates last month for the first time in three years.
In a statement , the Fed said economic activity is growing at a "strong pace" while acknowledging that inflation remains elevated.
"The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2% goal," Fed officials said.
Wall Street had forecast that the Fed would stand pat on rates. Investor reaction was muted, with the three major indexes remaining essentially flat after the Fed's announcement.
The Fed's benchmark rate is its main weapon for stabilizing consumer prices, which have crept up in recent months. The latest rate decision comes less than a week before Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections , where affordability issues will be top of mind for voters. President Trump has long urged the Fed to ease borrowing costs.
During a press conference after the rate decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said economic indicators are moving in the right direction, citing robust consumer spending, strong capital expenditures and healthy overall economic growth.
But he said inflation remains "too high" and acknowledged that the Fed hasn't yet succeeded in bringing inflation under control.
"On the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive, and yet Americans, of course, are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the committee's objective for close to six years," he told reporters. "It's our responsibility to get inflation down."
Ten members of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rates, voted to hold the benchmark rate steady. Two FOMC members — Fed Board Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank President Beth Hammack — voted to raise it by 0.25 percentage points.
"We just came out of a heck of a family fight, a serious, sober discussion," Warsh said Wednesday. "I think we came to the right policy decision for this moment."
Investors and Wall Street analysts widely expected the Fed to remain on hold in October, but many economists think policymakers will raise rates at their last meeting of the year in December and again in 2027.
"The two hawkish dissents, the wording of the policy statement, and prior comments from officials all suggest the central bank will hike rates in December," Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist for forecasting firm Oxford Economics, said in an email following the Fed's decision.
Samuel Tombs, chief U.S. economist at investment advisory firm Pantheon Macroeconomics, said financial markets are pricing in an additional 0.75 percentage points of tightening over the next year as the Fed tries to douse inflation.
Warsh demurred when asked if Fed officials would raise rates at their Dec. 8-9 meeting, citing his stated reluctance to telegraph his policy views.
"A lot of things can happen, so I'm not going to be able to share with you my musings about what happens when this group gets together six weeks from now," he told a reporter.
The Iran war has kept global energy costs elevated, making it harder to bring down prices in the U.S. Last month, the closely watched Consumer Price Index rose at a 3.7% annual rate ; core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.6% from a year ago. Both measures were above economists' expectations.
Solid economic growth and steady consumer spending are also exerting upward pressure on prices, complicating the task of taming inflation, according to economists.
The federal funds rate — what banks charge each other for overnight loans — influences the cost of borrowing across the U.S. economy. A rate hike can spur higher borrowing costs for bank loans, credit cards and auto loans, while boosting returns for savings accounts.
The Fed's pause in rate hikes could provide borrowers with some breathing room, Bankrate home lending expert Linda Bell said, citing potential relief for home equity rates. Still, consumers may be in for higher borrowing costs down the road. Matt Schulz, a chief consumer finance analyst at LendingTree, said it's possible some loan rates could continue to climb heading into the holiday shopping season.
"Even though the Fed is leaving rates alone this month, it might raise rates again at its last meeting of the year in December," Schulz said in an email ahead of the Fed's decision. "That is far from guaranteed, but it is something that Americans should be aware of. It means that the debt they run up during the holidays could get a little more expensive to pay off before the year ends, through no fault of their own."
While the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged was widely expected, Warsh elicited surprise by announcing changes to the central bank's meeting schedule.
Policymakers will continue to meet eight times throughout the year. But starting in 2027, one of those meetings will be reserved for discussion and strategizing on monetary policy, Warsh said. At that meeting, the Fed will not vote on interest rates or issue a policy statement.
By 2028, Warsh said he expects two meetings to be dedicated to policy discussion and six to issuing rate decisions.
The change aligns with Warsh's broader vision for the Fed. He has been vocal in arguing for more limited communication from Fed officials, known as forward guidance, to preserve their flexibility in setting policy.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular and information-rich intervals," he said. "But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons, focusing, as I say, on the left side of the decimal point."

articles.title_orig: Dutch Zookeeper Dies After Rare Mauling by a Leopard
articles.title_zh: Dutch Zookeeper Dies After Rare Mauling by a Leopard
articles.content_orig:
A zookeeper has died from her injuries days after she was attacked by a leopard at the Dutch safari park where she worked.
The unnamed employee, who had worked at the Beekse Bergen safari park for almost four decades, was attacked by the animal on Saturday and died on Tuesday.
“With enormous sadness, we have to report that the animal caretaker of safari park Beekse Bergen passed away today from the injuries she sustained on Saturday, October 24, in an incident with a leopard in the park,” the park said in a statement Tuesday.
“Her passing also deeply affects us all, and we are intensely grieving with her family, friends and loved ones. We ask for peace and privacy for her loved ones and our staff, so that they can process this profound loss,” the statement added.
The woman suffered serious wounds to her head and neck while working in an enclosure with two male Persian leopards, the Associated Press reported.
The woman contacted colleagues via a walkie talkie after the incident in the leopard’s enclosure and an ambulance and trauma helicopter were dispatched at around 11 a.m. local time Saturday, AP added. She underwent emergency surgery but her condition worsened on Sunday evening.
The employee joined the park, located in the southern Netherlands, when she was 17 years old and had worked there “with short breaks for almost 40 years,” the park’s statement added.
CNN affiliate NOS reported that the zookeeper had been working with the leopards for eight years and had been working alone in the enclosure with two male Persian leopards when she was attacked.
There are no cameras inside the enclosure, the park told NOS, which also reported that the animals have been treated as normal since the incident.
The park said that an independent investigation had been launched into the woman’s death.
Rhino kills zookeeper and seriously injures another in Austria
Home to more than 100 species of animals, Beekse Bergen offers visitors the choice of seeing the safari park by foot, car, bus and boat.
This is not the first time a member of staff at a zoo or safari park has been fatally injured by an animal.
In 2023, a zookeeper was killed in Austria after being attacked by a rhino. The incident, in which another zookeeper was injured, occurred at Salzburg Hellbrunn Zoo. Two years prior to that, a woman working at a safari park in Chile was killed by a tiger while working in the big cats’ enclosure.
CNN’s Rose Roobeek contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: War against Iran won’t distract America from China’s military buildup, Hegseth tells Pacific allies
articles.title_zh: War against Iran won’t distract America from China’s military buildup, Hegseth tells Pacific allies
articles.content_orig:
An Iranian flag is seen as missiles and air defense systems are displayed at Baharestan Square in Tehran, Iran, on September 29, 2026.
President Donald Trump’s conflict with Iran has become a political liability for his administration. Since the last U.S. strikes on Iran fell on Sept. 8, Trump has publicly ruled out attacking Iran before the November midterm elections—and promised to end the conflict after them.
Then, rumblings grew that U.S. and Israeli military planners had reportedly drawn up new strike options against Iran, including the possible use of the largest non-nuclear weapon in the American arsenal: the GBU-43/B, also dubbed “the Mother of All Bombs”.
The targets purportedly would be Iran’s nuclear facilities and energy infrastructure, though there are doubts about whether the bomb could penetrate Iran’s most deeply buried sites. According to these reports, Trump apparently is seeking a strike he could present as a military victory and then end the war without appearing to back down.
But such an approach risks triggering a far wider war than Washington intends. Tehran remains unlikely to let Washington end the conflict quickly and, fearing a potential attack from the U.S., could itself strike first. Either scenario could lead to a new round of fighting far more destructive than the last.
Reports of military plans involving “the mother of all bombs” came against the backdrop of two other worrying developments. First, Iran has been escalating its naval attacks, likely in response to increased flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Notably, two UAE-owned cargo ships, the GFS Pride and the Cape Dao , were struck in the Strait as part of this sharp uptick.
Secondly, diplomatic efforts appear to have hit a wall. In late September, Trump rejected the proposal Tehran had put forward on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly: an end to fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon; the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade and oil sanctions; the release of some of Iran’s frozen assets; and the reopening of Hormuz within seven days. Instead, Washington insists that Iran must take steps regarding its nuclear program as part of the package, something Iranian leaders say they will only do at a later stage.
The timing of any U.S.-Israeli attack remains uncertain. While Trump has said he will not resume attacks before the midterms, Israel held its election on Oct. 27, a week earlier, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had reportedly sought renewed fighting before both elections.
American and Israeli objectives may differ, of course. Trump appears to want something he can portray as a spectacular military victory without having to undergo another prolonged war, while Netanyahu’s rhetoric about “ finishing the job ” suggests more ambitious goals, potentially including toppling the Islamic Republic. Tehran seems to be preparing for either scenario with its own response: a prolonged, region-wide war designed to impose devastating economic costs.
The dominant perspective in Tehran is that the next war must be fought in a way that makes it so costly that a future U.S. president would not contemplate another. Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), said in late September that Iran “will not stop until we have driven the United States out of the region, punished the aggressor, and established permanent deterrence so that no one will dare attack Iran.”
That logic, should it prevail, rules out a symbolic, tit-for-tat exchange. In Tehran’s view, a limited American strike on Pickaxe Mountain , the fortified nuclear site near Natanz that Trump has repeatedly evoked, followed by a limited Iranian response, would send Washington precisely the wrong message: that it can attack Iran’s nuclear facilities, register domestic political gain, and pay a limited, acceptable cost. Iranian officials have therefore warned that even a symbolic, non-lethal strike would trigger a broad response, denying Trump the quick exit he may have asked of his war planners.
Under this scenario, Iran would target regional energy and economic infrastructure. “In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one will sell oil,” Ghalibaf has warned . The UAE is particularly exposed: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, has accused it of oil “ smuggling ” in cahoots with U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM). Rezaei also identified new potential targets: undersea cables, data centers, and AI infrastructure in the region, which he claims are worth “more than $2 trillion.” Ghalibaf subsequently extended the threat to regional governments and investors, threatening that anyone providing “funding, equity, land, or energy” to AI companies that “facilitate military aggression” against Iran “will face coercive action.”
If raising the cost of war is the first instrument in Iran’s calculus, duration is the second. Ali Balali , an adviser to the IRGC’s Aerospace Force commander, suggested Iran would conserve its arsenal in preparation for a prolonged confrontation, rather than expend it early. Two days later, Iranian Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia argued that the enemy’s weak point is a prolonged war.
Timing is a third dimension in Iranian thinking. Iranian military officials have increasingly mentioned the possibility of striking first, preemptively. Akraminia stated that if Iran were to conclude that an attack by the U.S. and/or Israel is imminent, “we will certainly engage in preemptive warfare.” Mehdi Mohammadi , strategic affairs adviser to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, went further, arguing that a successful strategy requires not only striking first but also delivering a decisive blow capable of “changing the balance.” There is thus at least the possibility that Iran might move early, and then fight long.
That could occur due to miscalculation resulting from ambiguous American and Israeli signals: leaked strike plans, carrier and amphibious deployments, and aircraft approaching but not entering Iranian airspace. Military experts in Iran see this pattern as an effort to normalize military activity and regain the element of surprise. Tehran could thus mistake military signaling for an imminent attack and strike preemptively, even though it may not want another round of war.
The fourth element concerns the range of those Tehran would hold responsible in the event of an attack. On Oct. 5 Ali Abdollahi , chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, declared that if the United States acted against Iran “directly or indirectly through Israel,” Iranian forces would retaliate against the United States. The warning carries more weight in the wake of Trump’s decision to openly back Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s election. Indeed, some in Tehran interpreted this as a signal that Washington would allow Israel to strike Iran after the midterms. As a result, Tehran has made clear that even were Israel to carry out the attack on its own, U.S. forces and assets in the region would face retaliation.
This interpretation suggests that the scope of Iran’s response to a U.S. strike likely would be far wider. Its conduct in Hormuz since late September offers a preview of how it could broaden the conflict. When the UAE, backed by CENTCOM, kept oil moving through a southern corridor along the Omani coast, the IRGC shifted its attacks from small shuttle tankers to supertankers and stated that vessels using the “illegal corridor” would be “pursued and interdicted across the region.” Strikes followed off the UAE coast and near Qatar. An escalation in the region could drive Iran to go after vital energy and other infrastructure across the Gulf.
Iran’s regional partners also could widen the conflict, although Tehran does not fully control their actions. In Yemen, the Houthis have already opened a second maritime front in the Red Sea, threatening shipping and increasing pressure on Saudi Arabia. articles.content_orig:
Microsoft shares rose 5% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business.
Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement .
Net income of $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, increased from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, in the same quarter of last year. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million impact from investing in OpenAI.
Free cash flow of $18.63 billion moved 27% lower. Cloud rival Alphabet showed negative free cash flow for the quarter, while Meta said last week that it went free cash flow negative .
Microsoft has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to accommodate artificial intelligence demand. The company had $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30%. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
For the first time in an earnings statement, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $32.32 billion, which would have represented growth of more than 44%. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
Microsoft reported results under two operating segments for the first time since 1998. For the past 11 years it had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
Agents and Infra gave Microsoft $76.80 billion of its revenue, which was up almost 25% and more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft cloud revenue beats estimates in sign that AI bet is paying off
articles.title_zh: Microsoft cloud revenue beats estimates in sign that AI bet is paying off
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business.
Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business.
The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported  $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue.
For Azure, Hood said she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus.
"We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," the company's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts.
Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue.
Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues.
"In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said.
Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time.
Microsoft will continue to generate free cash flow through the 2027 fiscal year, but the company will access additional sources of funding when it's attractive to do so, Hood said.
Microsoft's net income increased to $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million loss on its investment in OpenAI.
For the first time, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter, despite the delays from third-party providers.
Analysts polled by StreetAccount expected $32.32 billion. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
Microsoft reported results under two operating segments — Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.  For the past 11 years, the company had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
In Agents and Infra, revenue rose almost 25% to $76.8 billion, more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.
The number of people using the Microsoft 365 Copilot AI assistant is up 50% from last quarter, CEO Satya Nadella said on the call. The company did not disclose the number of paid seats. The recently announced high-end Microsoft 365 E7 productivity bundle now has millions of seats, Hood said.
Revenue in the Devices and Consumer business slipped 3% to $15.48 billion, beating the StreetAccount consensus of $15.05 billion. The unit includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers.
Sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%, as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. The company pointed to the end of support for Windows 10 last year and weak PC demand.
As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities.
Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 5:30 p.m. ET.
This story is developing. Please check back for updates.

articles.title_orig: With 90% of votes counted, Netanyahu bloc has 53 seats, Eisenkot’s 48; Arab parties surge to 19
articles.title_zh: With 90% of votes counted, Netanyahu bloc has 53 seats, Eisenkot’s 48; Arab parties surge to 19
articles.content_orig:
The leader of Israel’s Balad party has condemned the country’s main political leaders for refusing to form a coalition with Arab parties, even after a record showing in polls could make them kingmakers for the next parliament after no clear winner emerged.
Sami Abu Shehadeh told Al Jazeera that Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about a fifth of the population, are being treated as illegitimate partners despite their turnout.
“This is racism,” he said. “We are a legitimate elected leadership of the national minority. The vast majority of our people decided that we are their leadership.”
Arab parties are on course to win a record 19 seats, giving them potentially decisive leverage over the main political blocs. With 85 percent of the vote counted, Israel’s Central Elections Committee has Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc ahead with at least 53 seats, and the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot on 48.
Both are short of the 61 needed to govern. Netanyahu says Israelis chose a strong right-wing government, while Eisenkot says they voted for change.
Abu Shehadeh, who leads Balad, one of the Joint List’s three parties, was not a candidate.
Israel’s elections committee voted to disqualify him at the request of far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, who accused him of supporting the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack due to an article issued the following day in which Abu Shehadeh called it an “important historical event”.
Abu Shehadeh subsequently told the Supreme Court he did not support “armed struggle” but acknowledged that a paragraph in the article had been incorrectly worded. He said his intention was to call for moving the conflict towards a political process.
He withdrew in October after a majority of the Supreme Court panel appeared willing to approve the disqualification. He rejects the grounds and said the court had made clear that Israel has “two different judicial systems, one for the Jews and one for the Arabs”.
“We are very proud of the Arab Palestinian minority in Israel that went in this very high percentage of voting,” he told Al Jazeera. The community’s first promise to voters, he said, was to prevent “this gang of criminals” from returning to power, naming Netanyahu and far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Ben-Gvir. “So our first promise, we can keep it from now .”
Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, said Netanyahu “has scared off everybody from talking to the Palestinian Israeli parties”, leaving him best placed to “call the shots”. She said that Eisenkot and his allies have indicated that they want a Zionist government and “do not want to form a government” with the Arab parties, leaving them few options.
Danny Ayalon, a former Israeli ambassador to the United States, told Al Jazeera that turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel came in “really unprecedented numbers” and that the parties “are going to have some significant clout”.
Mathematically, he said, Eisenkot’s bloc could join forces with the two Arab parties and pass the threshold, though it would take “political wizardry”. Yousef Jabareen, who leads the Joint List, has said his alliance’s “hands are extended” to oust Netanyahu.
Abu Shehadeh set out what Palestinian citizens want from the next government.
“We are against genocide and we are against apartheid. We want to promote a different political alternative, one which is based on the values of freedom, justice and equality for both people who are living between the river and the sea.”
Of Netanyahu, he said: “Our problem … is that he is a war criminal.”
A UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October’s US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave.
The Hague-based International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in 2024 for war crimes during the Gaza war.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: US FTC demands Walmart, Uber, Delta and others hand over data on personalized pricing
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: US FTC demands Walmart, Uber, Delta and others hand over data on personalized pricing
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Trade Commission is demanding information from Walmart , Uber and seven other companies on whether and how they use consumers' personal data such as location, browsing history and income to set individual prices, wages and job offers, a senior FTC official told Reuters on Wednesday.
The FTC is flexing its consumer protection powers ahead of the U.S. congressional elections next week, as voters consistently rank the cost of living as the most important issue.
Target , along with app services Lyft , DoorDash and Instacart, and airlines Delta , United , JetBlue , are also receiving demands, the official said.
The FTC will use the information to eventually publish a study to help inform regulators and lawmakers about personalized pricing and wage setting practices.
The advance of algorithmic pricing technology, including tools that incorporate AI, has fueled concern that companies are able to set prices for shoppers on an individual basis in order to extract the maximum price each shopper would be willing to pay.
Personalized pricing strategies are difficult to observe from the outside, because they serve different prices to different people. The FTC study aims to fill in that knowledge gap, demanding comprehensive information about the tools, strategies, and data companies use as well as how they affect prices, wages and job offers.
Efforts by state lawmakers to ban personalized pricing, along with the use of algorithms to individually tailor wages, have taken off in recent years.
The National Retail Federation has criticized the laws and defended retailers' use of data-driven discounts as a means of incentivizing loyalty.
FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson has said personalizing pricing could violate consumer protection laws where consumers do not expect it and that companies should expect enforcement.
After the FTC called for public comment, hundreds of commenters urged the FTC to ban the practice outright. The FTC has said it does not have the authority to issue a blanket prohibition against the practice.

articles.title_orig: Iran sees only unacceptable ideas in latest mediation to end war, official says
articles.title_zh: Iran sees only unacceptable ideas in latest mediation to end war, official says
articles.content_orig:
Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem said Wednesday the Iran-backed Lebanese movement was not concerned with the results of Israel's election , vowing to continue its "resistance" against the neighbouring country no matter who wins.
With 85% of ballots counted, the right-wing bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had a slight lead over the main opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, but was still short of a majority after Tuesday's election.
"We do not concern ourselves with who governs Israel, but let it be perfectly clear that it cannot continue its occupation and must leave our land," Qassem said in a written statement.
"The resistance will continue ... and will stand up to the aggression directed against it and against Lebanon, and there is no room to discuss the disarmament" of Hezbollah "as long as the occupation persists and its aggression continues," he added.
The group, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by the two wars it has waged against Israel since 2023.
U.K. Treasury chief John Healey used his first budget Wednesday to offer households and businesses some support with energy bills this winter in the face of what he termed "global economic storms."
He said that his "choice in the budget today is to give families and businesses some breathing space now," as the consequences of the Middle East conflict play out.
"For families, that means higher prices at the pump, higher energy bills and higher mortgages," he said in his statement, one of the main dates of the parliamentary calendar. "For businesses, higher running costs and more expensive loans. And the impact is felt in the public finances, too."
Among the measures announced was a 100-pound ($133) one-off payment this winter for 20 million lower- and middle-income households, proportionately more of whom live in the electoral battlegrounds in northern England.
Other measures include the extension of a cut in the sales tax on electricity bills and the abolition of a charge paid on gas bills.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the Arab parties of stealing the election through widespread fraud and called on Shin Bet, Israel's security agency, to investigate.
"We demand from the police and the Shin Bet a thorough investigation into the election theft by the Arab parties and the full prosecution of the criminals," Netanyahu's Likud party shared on his X account , translated from Hebrew. "This is a serious blow to Israeli democracy and the voting rights of Israeli citizens. The law enforcement agencies must act with an iron fist and in an immediate manner."
Netanyahu's party leads in the latest vote counts , but all of the parties will fall short of the majority needed to control the Knesset, Israel's parliament. With 85% of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1%, according to official election data.
Local media projected 53 seats for the Likud party, 48 seats for the Yahar and other opposition parties and 19 seats for the Arab-led parties. In order to reach a majority (61 of 120 seats) and pick a prime minister, deals will have to be made.
Amid reports Iran had rejected the latest proposal for peace from Qatari intermediaries, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X that his country continues to review ideas for a diplomatic solution to the eight-month war.
"While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed," Araghchi wrote. "We remain in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries to review ideas that can ensure implementation of our 7-Day Plan in even less than a week."
The seven-day plan was presented to the U.S. shortly after the U.N. General Assembly in September. However, President Trump rejected the idea presented by Iran for a seven-day ceasefire and then phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Earlier Wednesday, a senior Iranian official denied Qatar had presented Tehran with a new peace proposal on Sunday, saying instead Qatar had only come with "unacceptable" ideas , Reuters reported.
A source had earlier reported there were concerns Israel could begin a new bombing campaign after its election, according to Reuters.
Kuwait summoned Iran's envoy in protest on Wednesday, after Tehran denied one of its citizens, sentenced to death in Kuwait, was involved in an assassination plot targeting a top government figure.
Earlier this week, two Kuwaiti judicial sources told the AFP news agency that the Gulf state had condemned three Shia men to death for plotting the assassination of Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Fahad al-Yousef, collaborating with Iran; and for membership in Hezbollah.
Iran's embassy in Kuwait said earlier Wednesday it "rejects the Kuwaiti government's claim regarding the involvement of an Iranian citizen in a plot to assassinate figures or in any other act that could harm Kuwaiti national security."
It added that the person in question had been outside Kuwait for 10 years.
It said it regretted a "negative approach towards Iran, manifested, among other things, in the repetition of flimsy and worn-out scenarios concerning Iranian interference in Kuwaiti affairs."
In response, Kuwait summoned Iranian ambassador Mohammad Toutounji over the statement, which it said "constituted blatant interference in the internal affairs of the State of Kuwait and an infringement upon its sovereignty and the independence of its judiciary."
Abdulredha Haydar Dahqani was among those who had been sentenced to death, the judicial sources told AFP.
Dahqani, an Iranian national, had already been handed the death penalty in 2016 after he was tried in absentia along with 25 Kuwaitis. He was convicted of spying for Iran and plotting attacks.
Another was Hussein Abdallah al-Maatouq, a religious dignitary and secretary-general of the National Islamic Alliance, Kuwait's most influential Shia movement, the sources said.
Israel's defense minister on Wednesday denounced opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot for urging the military to resist post-election pressure from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened new strikes on Iran.
"His call to senior military officials not to obey the directives of the prime minister or me or of other relevant security authorities, on the grounds that 'they have his support,' is an anti-democratic statement detached from reality," Israel Katz wrote on X .
Eisenkot, a former military chief, said in a speech to supporters after Tuesday's election that Netanyahu was a caretaker prime minister lacking a mandate and the military should serve the state rather than the premier.
"Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you. You have my unequivocal backing. Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said.
Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened in recent days to renew strikes on Iran.
Media reports, denied by Netanyahu, said military chief Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir pushed back immediately before the election on the prime minister's new plans on Iran.
Eisenkot's comments were the latest in "a campaign of lies" about tension between Netanyahu and the military over Iran, Katz said.
Yemen's Ministry of Transport has warned of risks to civil aviation safety after Aden International Airport was targeted in a missile attack attributed to the Houthi group for the sixth time, Saudi Arabia's Asharq News reported.
The missile strike shook parts of the southern city, raising fresh concerns over the safety of airport operations and the potential threat to civilian air traffic.
Airport authorities had evacuated all employees and workers from the facility following Houthi threats to target the airport.
Iran is finalizing a protocol with Russia to accelerate joint development of small modular nuclear reactors, Behrouz Kamalvandi, spokesman and deputy for international, legal and parliamentary affairs at the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, has announced.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Reports Quarterly Cloud Sales That Beat Estimates
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Reports Quarterly Cloud Sales That Beat Estimates
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business.
Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business.
The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported  $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases, because of "timing differences between receipt of goods and payment and a lower mix of finance leases."
Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue.
Free cash flow declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time.
Microsoft's net income increased to $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million loss on its investment in OpenAI.
For the first time, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter. Analysts polled by StreetAccount expected $32.32 billion. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
Microsoft reported results under two operating segments — Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.  For the past 11 years, the company had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
In Agents and Infra, revenue rose almost 25% to $76.8 billion, more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.
Revenue in the Devices and Consumer business slipped 3% to $15.48 billion, beating the StreetAccount consensus of $15.05 billion. The unit includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers.
Sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%, as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. The company pointed to the end of support for Windows 10 last year and weak PC demand.
As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities.
Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 5:30 p.m. ET.
This story is developing. Please check back for updates.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gestures as he speaks to supporters at Likud party headquarters in Jerusalem following the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. David Goldman/AP hide caption
Israel has held an important election– its first since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on that country. articles.title_orig: Exclusive | Nelson Peltz’s Trian Offers to Buy Wendy’s for $1.4 Billion
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | Nelson Peltz’s Trian Offers to Buy Wendy’s for $1.4 Billion
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Wendy's ( WEN ) may be cooking up burgers for a billionaire soon.
Longtime Wendy's investor and former chairman Nelson Peltz of Trian Partners has reportedly offered $1.4 billion to buy the struggling fast food giant , according to an SEC filing.
Wendy's shares rose 15% in early trading. The company's market cap was $1.17 billion prior to the deal.
A Wendy's spokesperson didn't return a request for comment. A spokesperson for Trian Partners didn't return a request for comment.
Billionaire Peltz — while familiar with the operations — would essentially be buying a dumpster fire.
After nearly two years of struggles competing with the likes of behemoths McDonald's ( MCD ) and Yum! Brands' ( YUM ) Taco Bell, plus upstarts such as Shake Shack ( SHAK ), Wendy's is on the cusp of a large number of restaurant closures.
"With one of its largest franchisees filing bankruptcy in September (although contested by WEN given prior termination of franchise agreement), we think investors likely expect closures to tick higher than expected, but we admit visibility on our side remains somewhat limited and there could still be a range of outcomes," veteran restaurant analyst Andy Barish warned in a recent note.
"That said," he added, "given our view that there are likely additional franchise operators in the system facing challenges with leveraged balance sheets, higher interest rates and profitability pressures from higher beef, labor & build costs (like many others in QSR), we think it is prudent to moderate our development estimates and bake in more potential closures over the next 6-12 months, as the company works to strengthen its system."
Meritage Hospitality Group, one of Wendy's largest franchise operators, with more than 300 locations, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September following severe margin pressures and an escalating dispute with corporate headquarters. The company reportedly initiated plans to shutter at least 41 locations. Reports emerged this week that it could close up to 60.
The high-profile bankruptcy only added grease to the smoldering fire that is the Wendy's restaurant base.
Franchisees had already been closing their locations and heading for the hills.
Buried inside Wendy's brutal second quarter earnings call was a mention that 289 locations closed in the US during the first half of the year.
There are about 5,700 Wendy's in the US, and Barish estimated the Wendy's US store base will be around 5,600 by the end of 2027.
The decision on how many more locations will be closed falls on new CEO Bob Wright, who hasn't hidden his view that Wendy's needs to focus on more profitable locations.
Wright officially took over as CEO on May 21, adding to the yawning list of executive turnover at the fast food chain over the past two years. He is a seasoned fast food exec who spent the previous five years fixing Potbelly as CEO. Wright's appointment marked a return to Wendy's, where he previously served in several senior leadership roles, including COO.
Wright has his work cut out for him in saving Wendy's beyond tightening up the store base count.
Wendy's has posted six straight quarters of same-store sales declines, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace analysis.

articles.title_orig: Perv teacher learns fate for sex with 2 students — that already ended her job and marriage
articles.title_zh: Perv teacher learns fate for sex with 2 students — that already ended her job and marriage
articles.content_orig:
A married teacher in Australia was on Wednesday sentenced to just over a year in jail for having sex with two teenage students — which she tried to blame on “irresistible” impulses driven by bipolar disorder.
Tayla Lee Brailey , 32, wept as she hugged her parents and several supporters at her sentencing in Sydney on Wednesday — after already having lost her job and her husband after admitting her twisted crimes, Australian outlet ABC reported .
Brailey was first arrested in August 2024 for having sex with a 17-year-old boy in her car, returning to her classes after the sordid hookup.
She was released on bail — just to be busted again a few weeks later when it emerged she’d also touched a 16-year-old student’s genitals in her classroom, an experience that he said in a victim statement still overwhelms him with shame.
Brailey had groomed that younger victim online, according to the Canberra Times , sending him a naked picture of her in the shower and asking, “Do you like what you see?”
She then made him send her a nude in return. “Yum,” she replied to the 16-year-old student. “Stay back with me after school,” she wrote — with them kissing and touching each other’s genitals in her classroom.
“He has been feeling ashamed and had to leave high school before he finished … because of the shame he felt,” the judge, Justice Elizabeth Ryan, said during Bailey’s sentencing.
“He had suffered lack of sleep and flashbacks … he said none of his friends at high school speak to him anymore.”
The judge was told that Brailey was later diagnosed with bipolar disorder, creating impaired judgment and increased sex drive, leaving her with an “irresistible impulse” for sex with the boys, as the Australian also reported.
The judge, however, said that while Brailey’s crimes may have been “terrible mistakes,” she “used her position as a teacher … to abuse the trust of two young persons.”
“It is also relevant that she knew what she was doing was wrong but persisted with it,” Judge Ryan said.
“Offences like this cause immense harm to the trust that must exist between families and the education system,” the judge said.
“For these reasons … no penalty other than imprisonment is appropriate.”
Brailey was sentenced to nine months in prison for having sex with the 17-year-old student, and a year for sexually touching the 16-year-old boy, with an aggregate term of 15 months in jail.
She will also be placed on the child protection register for 15 years.
The teacher — who has since trained as an accountant — will be eligible for parole in April 2027.
